messages.content: Explain why a metal spoon feels colder than a wooden spoon when both are at room temperature. Answer in two to four sentences of plain prose.

message.content: Both spoons are actually at the same temperature, but the metal one feels colder because metal is a much better conductor of heat than wood. When you touch the metal spoon, it rapidly draws heat away from your skin, and your nerves register that heat loss as "cold." The wooden spoon conducts heat poorly, so warmth stays near the surface of your fingers and it feels closer to neutral.
